cards.front: What should you know about drama exam tips?
cards.back: Structure each portfolio section using: What we did → Why we chose this approach → How we developed it → What effect we intended → How the audience responded → What we would improve. This systematic approach ensures full AO4 coverage.
Visual record of process (e.g. Concrete, specific)
Live process, performance quality (e.g. Authentic, dynamic)
Breadth and depth of investigation (e.g. Demonstrates rigour)

Students often make mistakes here. Wrong: The portfolio is just a record of what happened in rehearsals — you just need to describe the process. Correct: The portfolio is an EVALUATIVE document. Describing what happened earns basic marks; explaining WHY choices were made, HOW they developed the piece, and EVALUATING their effectiveness earns top marks. Every paragraph should contain analysis, not
Write a portfolio entry evaluating how you used a practitioner's ideas to develop a key moment in your devised piece.

The devising portfolio is assessed on AO4 (analyse and evaluate — 30% of the devising component). Marks are awarded for: research and exploration (how you developed ideas), development and refinement (how you improved the piece), and evaluation (how you assess the final outcome). The portfolio must show analytical depth, not just chronological description.
